scope: Exact equipment-method candidates, independent Main review required before release. Original recipes/nutrition/quantities/prices remain unchanged.

originalSteps.instruction: Put long-grain white rice, water for cooking starch in the lidded saucepan. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for about 15-20 minutes until the rice is tender and water is absorbed. Turn off and rest covered 5 minutes. Cook the filling on the second burner while the rice cooks. Use the stated dry rice weight, not a cooked-weight substitution.

Cut boneless skinless chicken breast into strips no thicker than 1 cm; do not rinse raw poultry. Heat the allocated olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add the chicken with garlic powder, table salt and cook about 8-12 minutes, turning, until several thick centers reach 165 F (74 C). Transfer every cooked piece and its measured pan juices to the clean heatproof filling bowl. Keep this bowl separate from raw-food utensils.

Return all cooked boneless skinless chicken breast from the clean heatproof filling bowl to the skillet. Take the skillet off the heat and let bubbling stop. Fold in all lemon juice. Serve all cooked rice with the complete filling and sauce, divided into two portions.

Add no unlisted oil, water or food. Reheat the filling too if it has cooled; retain every cooked ingredient and measured juice. Then follow the original finishing order and serve promptly. originalSteps.instruction: Bring the allocated water to a boil in the saucepan. Add plain dried wheat noodles and boil at the package timing, stirring and testing until tender. Drain through the colander; this water is discarded. Keep the cooked starch in the emptied saucepan for assembly. Cook the filling on the second burner during this step.

Cut boneless skinless chicken breast into strips no thicker than 1 cm; do not rinse raw poultry. Heat the allocated olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add the chicken with garlic powder and cook about 8-12 minutes, turning, until several thick centers reach 165 F (74 C). Transfer every cooked piece and its measured pan juices to the clean heatproof filling bowl. Keep this bowl separate from raw-food utensils.

Keep the cooked protein in its clean bowl. Prepare broccoli, carrot in the skillet. Use the listed prepared cuts. Heat the oil allocated to this step over medium-low. Cook for about 5-10 minutes, stirring, until the produce is tender and hot. Lower the heat if the pan catches; no extra oil is needed.

Return all cooked boneless skinless chicken breast from the clean heatproof filling bowl to the skillet. Take the skillet off the heat and let bubbling stop. Whisk all ready-made smooth peanut butter, reduced-sodium soy sauce, lime juice together in the now-empty clean heatproof filling bowl until smooth, then fold every portion of that sauce through the hot filling. Add all cooked plain dried wheat noodles from the saucepan and toss until evenly coated. Divide into two portions.

After scraping all measured filling and juices into the clean bowl, let the empty skillet cool enough to clean safely, then wash and dry it. Set it over medium-low heat with no added oil. Toast one or two bread slices in one flat layer, without crowding, for about 1-3 minutes per side until lightly golden and crisp; turn with the spatula and lower the heat if browning too fast. Transfer each batch to a clean plate and repeat for all four slices. Switch off the burner before assembly. Keep the cooked filling covered in its clean heatproof bowl during the brief toast batches; if it cools, reheat it to 165 F (74 C) before adding the original finishing sauce and serving. Combine all lemon juice with the hot filling in the clean bowl. Divide the complete filling between two toast sandwiches. Use no extra butter or spread.

Turn off the burner. Put the saucepan on a stable heatproof surface, covered and separate from raw-food utensils. Use the single free burner for the skillet next; no parallel pan heating is needed. At assembly, if the starch has cooled, reheat it gently in its saucepan on this same burner, stirring until 165 F (74 C), before adding the off-heat sauce or ready-to-eat toppings. Add no unlisted oil, water or food. Reheat the filling too if it has cooled; retain every cooked ingredient and measured juice. Then follow the original finishing order and serve promptly.

Use thawed, peeled, tailless shrimp. Heat the allocated olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Cook with garlic powder about 2-3 minutes per side until every center is pearly and opaque, with no translucent flesh. Transfer every cooked piece and its measured pan juices to the clean heatproof filling bowl. Keep this bowl separate from raw-food utensils.

Keep the cooked protein in its clean bowl. Prepare Pineapple canned in juice in the skillet. Use the listed prepared cuts. Heat the oil allocated to this step over medium-low. Cook for about 4-7 minutes, stirring, until the produce is tender and hot. Lower the heat if the pan catches; no extra oil is needed.

Return all cooked peeled deveined shrimp from the clean heatproof filling bowl to the skillet. Add Ready-to-serve teriyaki sauce to the skillet. Warm gently over low heat for about 2-4 minutes, stirring until the filling is evenly coated and hot.

Fold every portion of the cooked plain dried wheat noodles from the saucepan into the skillet filling. Toss gently until coated and hot throughout. Include the complete cooked yield of the measured dry amount.
Take the skillet off the heat and let bubbling stop. Divide the complete skillet meal into two portions.

originalSteps.instruction: Start preheating the oven to 400 F (200 C) with a middle rack and the listed shallow ovenproof dish ready. Preheating overlaps ingredient preparation.

Put long-grain white rice, water for cooking starch in the lidded saucepan. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for about 15-20 minutes until the rice is tender and water is absorbed. Turn off and rest covered 5 minutes. Cook the filling on the second burner while the rice cooks. Use the stated dry rice weight, not a cooked-weight substitution.

Check the fish for bones and cut into 1 cm pieces. Combine the raw seafood with all oil and seasonings allocated to this step in the raw-food bowl. Cover and keep refrigerated while preparing the other filling. Do not pan-cook it now; it will cook once in the final oven step. Keep this raw bowl separate from the clean cooked-food holding bowl.

Prepare Canned sweetcorn in the skillet. Use the listed prepared cuts. Heat the oil allocated to this step over medium-low. Cook for about 4-7 minutes, stirring, until the produce is tender and hot. Lower the heat if the pan catches; no extra oil is needed.
Add ready-made mild tomato salsa, ready-made plain tomato sauce to the skillet. Warm gently over low heat for about 2-4 minutes, stirring until the filling is evenly coated and hot.

Fold every portion of the cooked long-grain white rice from the saucepan into the skillet filling. Toss gently until coated and hot throughout. Include the complete cooked yield of the measured dry amount.

Only now take the prepared raw seafood, its measured oil and seasonings from the covered raw-food bowl in the refrigerator. Fold every portion into the other filling. Keep raw utensils away from ready-to-eat toppings; wash them and the raw bowl after assembly. Transfer the complete already-combined filling and starch from the skillet to the shallow ovenproof dish and scatter all allocated cheese on top. Bake at 400 F (200 C) for about 15-20 minutes until bubbling, cheese is melted and the center reaches 165 F (74 C).

Turn off the burner. Put the saucepan on a stable heatproof surface, covered and separate from raw-food utensils. Use the single free burner for the skillet next; no parallel pan heating is needed. At assembly, if the starch has cooled, reheat it gently in its saucepan on this same burner, stirring until 165 F (74 C), before adding the off-heat sauce or ready-to-eat toppings. Add no unlisted oil, water or food. Reheat the filling too if it has cooled; retain every cooked ingredient and measured juice. Then follow the original finishing order and serve promptly.

Heat the allocated olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add Cooked reduced-fat turkey breakfast sausage and heat gently until hot. Refrigerated cooked meat being reheated must reach 165 F (74 C). Transfer every cooked piece and its measured pan juices to the clean heatproof filling bowl. Keep this bowl separate from raw-food utensils.

Return all cooked Cooked reduced-fat turkey breakfast sausage from the clean heatproof filling bowl to the skillet. Add Ready-to-serve basil pesto to the skillet. Turn the heat off and gently stir through the hot filling; do not fry or boil the pesto.

Fold every portion of the cooked plain dried short pasta from the saucepan into the skillet filling. Toss gently until coated and hot throughout. Include the complete cooked yield of the measured dry amount.
Take the skillet off the heat and let bubbling stop. Fold in all Low-moisture whole-milk mozzarella. Divide the complete skillet meal into two portions.

originalSteps.instruction: Start with refrigerated milk/dairy and chilled fresh fruit. Use fruit in its listed peeled/trimmed edible state, not unweighed whole fruit or an assumed frozen-weight substitution. Put every measured ingredient in the blender. Blend until smooth, scraping only with the motor stopped. This is a thick spoonable breakfast, not a juice with discarded pulp. Divide all mixture between two bowls and serve promptly; add no unlisted ice, syrup, toppings or liquid.

steps.instruction: Start with refrigerated milk/dairy and chilled fresh fruit. Use fruit in its listed peeled/trimmed edible state, not unweighed whole fruit or an assumed frozen-weight substitution. Use successive cold batches instead of filling a 1.5 litre jug at once. Before loading, check the actual blender instructions for thick mixtures, its maximum fill line, minimum working load and permitted ingredients; for the almond version it must be suitable for sliced nuts. Do not use a machine that cannot process these ingredients without extra liquid. Start by weighing half of EACH listed ingredient for each of two batches, keeping the remaining measured ingredients refrigerated. If that combination exceeds the permitted fill, split EVERY ingredient fraction equally again before loading, keeping the same proportions in every batch; never infer volume from grams. Load the allocated dairy first and then the fruit and remaining ingredients as permitted by the machine instructions. Secure the lid, blend only the permitted load and stop the motor before scraping. Stop if the blades stall or the motor strains; do not force it or add unlisted liquid. Transfer all of each smooth batch evenly between the two serving bowls, scraping out with the motor stopped and keeping the bowls chilled between batches. Repeat with every measured fraction, leaving no ingredients unused and discarding no pulp. Blend until smooth, scraping only with the motor stopped. This is a thick spoonable breakfast, not a juice with discarded pulp. Divide all mixture between two bowls and serve promptly; add no unlisted ice, syrup, toppings or liquid.

timingNotes: About 10-15 minutes active and elapsed with ingredients already refrigerated; chilling time is additional if needed. Untested estimate.

Respect the actual machine duty cycle/cooling instructions; keep dairy/fruit refrigerated during waits and serve promptly.
